meta.description: Levita, by Bit-A: a plugin with six pedals, worship and gospel presets, a tuner and a stage mode. It runs today on Linux as a CLAP plugin.

Levita.title: Levita, a bass rig for worship
Levita.lead: Levita comes with worship tones ready to play and an echo that follows the tempo: open it, pick a sound and play. The plugin is called Bass Rig, and it comes with a small DAW for recording rehearsals.

facts.runs: Runs today on Linux, as a CLAP plugin
facts.beta: Free beta in preparation, with a waitlist

board.alt: The Bass Rig pedalboard: six pedals in a row, Compressor, Octave, Drive, Chorus, Echo and Hammer, each with its knobs and footswitch. Above them are the Gospel preset, the Save, Save as and Stage buttons, the tuner and the output knob.
board.caption: A real capture of the Bass Rig pedalboard with the Gospel preset loaded. The interface is still in progress.
board.region: Capture of the Bass Rig pedalboard
board.hint: Swipe to see all six pedals

features.label: What it does
features.title: Less setup, more playing
features.lead: We focus on one genre, worship, and on having the sound ready when you get to rehearsal. Each card says what exists today and what is still missing.

presets.title: Worship and gospel presets
presets.text: Factory sounds for bass, made to sit under the band while people sing. You can also save and delete your own.

echo.title: Echo in tempo
echo.text: The echo syncs by note value, including the dotted eighth so common in worship, with a tape character.

pedalboard.title: Pedalboard with knobs
pedalboard.text: Its own interface with knobs, pedals you can reorder by dragging and a preset bar, inside the same plugin.

tuner.title: Tuner in the plugin
tuner.text: It shows the nearest note and whether you are sharp or flat. It listens to the instrument before the pedals, reaches the low B of a five-string bass and uses A = 440 Hz.

stage.title: Stage mode
stage.text: One big button per preset, with pages and keyboard shortcuts, for changing sounds without menus in the middle of a service.

remote.title: Control from your phone
remote.text: From the phone's browser: play and stop, change songs, mute tracks, master volume and the rig's knobs. It only answers on the same computer (the phone connects over USB with adb), unless you open it to the network.

latency.title: Low latency by design
latency.text: An audio path that allocates no memory in real time. The total latency with a real audio interface is still to be measured.

daw.title: A DAW for recording rehearsals
daw.text: Several tracks, a metronome with its own output, tap tempo and a count-in before recording.

pedals.label: The rig
pedals.title: Six pedals of our own design
pedals.lead: All of them are our own design, with no third-party code or models. Where published research exists, we follow it and cite it.

compressor.text: A soft-knee compressor with a logarithmic detector.

octave.text: Octaves down, with no pitch detector.

drive.text: Saturation with two characters and antialiasing.
drive.basedOn: Based on Parker et al., 2016 and Bilbao et al., 2017

chorus.text: A modulated delay line, in the classic style.
chorus.basedOn: Our own design, with no published work behind it

echo.text: A tape echo in tempo, with optional hysteresis.

hammer.text: A three-band preamp with adjustable mids.
hammer.basedOn: Bristow-Johnson filters; the rest is our own design

references.intro: We use these published works for the techniques of each pedal. The circuits, the values and the final tuning are our own design, and they are tuned by ear.

notes.bilbao2017: The first-order antialiasing form used in the saturation.
notes.chowdhury2019: The echo's tape loss response and hysteresis saturation.
notes.cookbook: The equalizer filters of the saturation and the preamp.

stage.label: Live
stage.title: One big button per preset
stage.body: Stage mode shows the presets as big buttons, with pages and keyboard shortcuts, for changing sounds without menus in the middle of a service.
stage.alt: Bass Rig's stage mode: five big buttons, one per preset, with Gospel selected.
stage.caption: A real capture of stage mode, with two factory presets and three sample ones.

platforms.label: Platforms
platforms.title: Where it runs
platforms.note: There are no plans for macOS for now.

roadmap.label: Roadmap
roadmap.title: What comes next, in order
roadmap.lead: It is a direction, not a promise: there are no dates.

interface.title: Pedalboard, presets and tuner
interface.text: Finish the rig's interface and test it inside the DAW.

beta.title: Public free beta
beta.text: First the waitlist with three tone videos, then the open beta, and finally the paid launch.

amp.title: Amp and cabinet
amp.text: Amp models and cabinet response, using only material we can legally distribute. Not implemented yet.

reverb.title: Reverb and ambience
reverb.text: A reverb with an ambient mode for wide worship sounds. Not implemented yet.

windows.title: Windows and VST3
windows.text: A Windows version and the VST3 format, to reach most computers.

closing.title: Need a plugin for your brand?
closing.body: What we learned building Levita goes into our contract work: audio processing, presets and interface.

meta.title: Acordes Finos, the harmony behind every progression
meta.description: Acordes Finos, by Bit-A: a harmony app for Android and the web. It shows the notes of each chord, its basses and inversions, the key, and the reason behind each change.

AcordesFinos.title: Acordes Finos, the harmony behind every progression
AcordesFinos.lead: You pick the chords of a progression and the app shows the notes of each one, its possible basses, the key, and why each change works.
AcordesFinos.status: Test version. Coming soon to Google Play.

actions.site: Visit the Acordes Finos site (in Spanish)

AcordesFinos.apkNote: It is a test version for Android 7 or later. Once the app is on Google Play, you will have to uninstall this one to install the store version.
AcordesFinos.heroShotAlt: The progression Cmaj7, Am7, Dm7, G7 in the app, with the key of C major and the Cmaj7 card: its notes C, E, G and B, each with its interval.

features.label: What it shows
features.title: Everything comes from the chords you pick
features.lead: 12 root notes and 16 chord types, from the major triad to the 13 and the 7b9.

notes.title: Every chord, note by note
notes.text: Notes are spelled the way a musician spells them, with the interval from the root and the construction in semitones. Cm is C Eb G, D is D F# A and C°7 is C Eb Gb Bbb.
notes.alt: The chord picker with the root G and the type 7 selected, and the Add G7 button.
notes.caption: The picker: root, chord type, and sharp or flat.

changes.title: The reason behind each change
changes.text: Between two chords, the app shows the root movement, the notes in common, how many semitones the voices move, and a smoothness score from 0 to 10, with an explanation of the harmonic movement.
changes.alt: The step from Cmaj7 to Am7, opened: the root goes down a minor third, the common notes are C, E and G, and an explanation of the movement.
changes.caption: From Cmaj7 to Am7: three notes in common.

basses.title: Basses and inversions
basses.text: Each chord lists its bass options, from root position to every inversion, with the character of each. For the whole progression it suggests bass lines. It also detects the likely key and names each chord accordingly.
basses.alt: The four bass options of G7: root position, G7/B in first inversion, G7/D in second and G7/F in third, each with its character.
basses.caption: The four bass options of G7.

songs.title: Songs in sections
songs.text: Progressions are saved in songs, ordered by section: intro, verse, pre-chorus, chorus, bridge, solo, outro and coda. Sections can be edited, reordered and deleted.
songs.alt: The song Balada en G with its sections: intro, verse 1, pre-chorus, chorus, a chorus variant and bridge, each with its chords.
songs.caption: A song with six sections, one of them a chorus variant.

audience.label: Who it is for
audience.title: For people who play, write, arrange or study
audience.body: Use it to see which notes a chord has, pick a bass, or understand why a progression sounds the way it does. Chords use letter names (C, D, E, F, G, A, B), and the app's interface is in Spanish.

promises.label: No surprises
promises.title: Free, offline and with no data collected

free.title: Free
free.text: It costs nothing, asks for no account and has no ads.

offline.title: No internet
offline.text: The Android app works offline, and the Google Play version does not ask for internet access. The web version does need a connection to open.

noServer.title: No server
noServer.text: There is no analytics and no sign-up, and the app sends nothing by itself: songs are stored on the phone.

closing.title: Need an app for musicians?
closing.body: Acordes Finos is a sample of what we do: musical logic, a clear interface and nothing the user did not ask for.

paragraphs.1: I played music for years, and the harmony of worship songs always struck me. Something sounded incredible and I did not know what it was, until I started playing bass because the band had no bass player.
paragraphs.2: That is when I understood its role: the part nobody hears clearly, but that holds everything together and makes everything sound right.
paragraphs.3: Bit-A makes that kind of piece: software nobody sees on stage and that makes the music sound. That is why our main product is a bass rig for worship.

intro.title: Your privacy is important to us
intro.content: It is Bit-A's policy to respect your privacy regarding any information we may collect while operating our website. This Privacy Policy applies to bit-a.com (hereinafter, "us", "we", or "bit-a.com"). We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting personally identifiable information you may provide us through the Website. We have adopted this privacy policy to explain what information may be collected on our Website, how we use this information, and under what circumstances we may disclose the information to third parties.

visitors.title: Website visitors
visitors.content: Like most website operators, Bit-A collects non-personally-identifying information of the sort that web browsers and servers typically make available, such as the browser type, language preference, referring site, and the date and time of each visitor request. Bit-A's purpose in collecting non-personally identifying information is to better understand how Bit-A's visitors use its website.

pii.title: Personally-identifying information
pii.content: Certain visitors to Bit-A's websites choose to interact with Bit-A in ways that require Bit-A to gather personally-identifying information. The amount and type of information that Bit-A gathers depends on the nature of the interaction.

security.title: Security
security.content: The security of your Personal Information is important to us, but remember that no method of transmission over the Internet, or method of electronic storage is 100% secure. While we strive to use commercially acceptable means to protect your Personal Information, we cannot guarantee its absolute security.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.content: To enrich and perfect your online experience, Bit-A uses "Cookies", similar technologies and services provided by others to display personalized content, appropriate advertising and store your preferences on your computer.

changes.title: Privacy policy changes
changes.content: Although most changes are likely to be minor, Bit-A may change its Privacy Policy from time to time, and in Bit-A's sole discretion. Bit-A encourages visitors to frequently check this page for any changes to its Privacy Policy.
